GLOSSARY.RO: Responsible Official — the Local Chief Executive (City Mayor) who sets policy and priorities and delegates authority to the Incident Commander (NDRRMC MC No. 4, s. 2012).
GLOSSARY.IC: Incident Commander — overall on-scene manager of the incident, acting under a delegation of authority from the RO.
GLOSSARY.UC: Unified Command — two or more agencies with jurisdiction share command and agree one set of objectives (e.g., CDRRMO with PCG at sea, or BFP for fire).
GLOSSARY.ICP: Incident Command Post — where the IC and Command Staff work on scene. Different from the EOC.
GLOSSARY.IMT: Incident Management Team — the IC plus Command and General Staff. It is the "resource employer"; response clusters are the "resource providers" (NDRRMC Memo Nos. 43 & 44, s. 2016; Memo No. 131, s. 2018).
GLOSSARY.IAP: Incident Action Plan — objectives, strategies and assignments for one operational period, approved by the IC.
GLOSSARY.EOC: Emergency Operations Center — a facility staffed and equipped to coordinate stakeholders, manage information and mobilize resources in anticipation of or in support of incident operations (NDRRMC Memo No. 131, s. 2018). It must not be co-located with the ICP.
GLOSSARY.ICS: Incident Command System — standard on-scene, all-hazards management system adopted under NDRRMC MC No. 4, s. 2012.
GLOSSARY.CDRRMO: City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (RA 10121, Sec. 12).
GLOSSARY.CDRRMC: City DRRM Council, chaired by the City Mayor. Recommends declarations and approves major actions.
GLOSSARY.BDRRMC: Barangay DRRM Committee — first line of warning, evacuation and reporting in each of Ormoc's 85 barangays.
GLOSSARY.RDRRMC: Regional DRRM Council — for Ormoc, RDRRMC 8 (Eastern Visayas), with OCD Region VIII as secretariat.
GLOSSARY.OCD: Office of Civil Defense — secretariat of the NDRRMC; OCD Region VIII covers Leyte.
GLOSSARY.NDRRMC: National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council.
GLOSSARY.PDRA: Pre-Disaster Risk Assessment — structured assessment of the forecast hazard, exposure and needed actions, done before impact (NDRRMC Memo No. 17, s. 2014).
GLOSSARY.RDANA: Rapid Damage Assessment and Needs Analysis — done in the first hours to days after impact to set relief and recovery priorities.
GLOSSARY.TCWS: Tropical Cyclone Wind Signal (PAGASA), Nos. 1–5. Higher numbers mean stronger winds and shorter lead time.
GLOSSARY.PAGASA: Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration — the official source of weather, rainfall and storm-surge warnings.
GLOSSARY.PHIVOLCS: Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology — the official source of earthquake and tsunami information.
GLOSSARY.PEIS: PHIVOLCS Earthquake Intensity Scale, I to X. Intensity VII is "destructive".
GLOSSARY.LDRRMF: Local DRRM Fund — at least 5% of estimated regular revenue. 70% for prevention, mitigation and preparedness; 30% Quick Response Fund (RA 10121, Sec. 21). Unexpended balances go to the Special Trust Fund.
GLOSSARY.QRF: Quick Response Fund — the 30% of the LDRRMF for relief and recovery, usable once a state of calamity is declared.
GLOSSARY.AA: Anticipatory action — action before impact under RA 12287. LGUs may charge it to no more than 10% of the 70% LDRRMF, plus the Special Trust Fund, donor or ODA funds; not the QRF. Under 3 days lead time up to 70% of the AA allocation may be disbursed; beyond 3 days, at most 30%.
GLOSSARY.SitRep: Situation Report — cumulative status report to higher councils. Eastern Visayas LGUs use the harmonized template of RDRRMC 8 Res. No. 12-006, s. 2023: under Blue or Red alert, LGU reports are due by 09:00 and 19:00.
GLOSSARY.DROMIC: Disaster Response Operations Monitoring and Information Center — DSWD's report on affected and displaced families.
GLOSSARY.CCCM: Camp Coordination and Camp Management — the cluster for evacuation centers (DSWD-led).
GLOSSARY.WASH: Water, Sanitation and Hygiene — part of the Health cluster.
GLOSSARY.MDM: Management of the Dead and Missing — DILG-led cluster (NDRRMC MC No. 19, s. 2016).
GLOSSARY.SRR: Search, Rescue and Retrieval cluster (AFP-led at national level).
GLOSSARY.WASAR: Water Search and Rescue — teams trained and equipped for flood and swift-water rescue.
GLOSSARY.USAR: Urban Search and Rescue — teams trained for collapsed-structure rescue.
GLOSSARY.MCI: Mass Casualty Incident — casualties exceed the normal capacity of local responders and hospitals (DOH AO No. 155, s. 2004).
GLOSSARY.START: Simple Triage and Rapid Treatment — sorts casualties into Red (immediate), Yellow (delayed), Green (minor) and Black (dead/expectant).
GLOSSARY.PCG: Philippine Coast Guard — leads maritime search and rescue and maritime safety.
GLOSSARY.BFP: Bureau of Fire Protection — fire, hazmat and rescue.
GLOSSARY.PNP: Philippine National Police — Law and Order cluster lead; in Ormoc, the Ormoc City Police Office.
GLOSSARY.AFP: Armed Forces of the Philippines — SRR cluster lead nationally; provides augmentation on request.
GLOSSARY.CSWDO: City Social Welfare and Development Office — runs evacuation centers and relief locally.
GLOSSARY.DSWD: Department of Social Welfare and Development — Vice-Chair for Response; leads FNI, CCCM and Protection clusters.
GLOSSARY.DOH: Department of Health — Health cluster lead.
GLOSSARY.DILG: Department of the Interior and Local Government — leads the MDM cluster; Operation L!sto preparedness protocols.
GLOSSARY.DepEd: Department of Education — Education cluster lead; schools are often used as evacuation centers.
GLOSSARY.OBO: Office of the Building Official — inspects structures before re-occupancy.
GLOSSARY.CENRO: City Environment and Natural Resources Office.
GLOSSARY.EMB: Environmental Management Bureau (DENR) — air-quality and pollution authority.
GLOSSARY.PIO: Public Information Officer — Command Staff position; the single source of incident information to media and the public.
GLOSSARY.SOFR: Safety Officer — Command Staff position with authority to stop unsafe acts.
GLOSSARY.LOFR: Liaison Officer — Command Staff position; the contact point for assisting and cooperating agencies.
GLOSSARY.EC: Evacuation center. RA 12076 (Ligtas Pinoy Centers Act) provides for dedicated, resilient evacuation centers.
GLOSSARY.H2S: Hydrogen sulfide — toxic, flammable gas from geothermal fluids. Heavier than air, it pools in low ground; high concentrations deaden the sense of smell.
GLOSSARY.PFD: Personal flotation device (life vest). Required for anyone working on or near flood water.
GLOSSARY.ETC: Emergency Telecommunications cluster — radio, satellite and backup communications.
GLOSSARY.MARINA: Maritime Industry Authority — regulates vessels and shipping.
GLOSSARY.EPR: Emergency Preparedness and Response protocols for slow-onset hazards in the RDRRMOC SOPG: Standby (green), ALPHA (yellow), BRAVO (orange), CHARLIE (red).
GLOSSARY.SWB: Severe Weather Bulletin (PAGASA) — issued for tropical cyclones; a trigger for raising EOC alert levels.
GLOSSARY.DORMS: Disaster Online Reporting and Monitoring System — part of the harmonized reporting contents.
GLOSSARY.GIDA: Geographically Isolated and Disadvantaged Areas — communities cut off by distance, terrain or weather; warnings and aid must reach them deliberately.
GLOSSARY.DVI: Disaster Victim Identification — process that turns unidentified remains into confirmed, identified dead.
GLOSSARY.NIMT: NDRRMC Incident Management Team — a deployable national IMT that can augment or assume management of complex incidents.
GLOSSARY.RIT: Rapid Intervention Team — a standby team that rescues responders in trouble.
GLOSSARY.COP: Common Operating Picture — one shared, verified view of the situation used by all sections and agencies.
GLOSSARY.PSCP: Public Service Continuity Plan — keeps essential City services running during disruption (OCD PSCP Guidebook).
GLOSSARY.ACDV: Accredited Community Disaster Volunteers — trained volunteers accredited through the LDRRMO; mobilized under RA 12287 IRR Rule IV, Sec. 5.
GLOSSARY.CBMS: Community-Based Monitoring System — household registry used to target social amelioration under RA 12287.
GLOSSARY.MGB: Mines and Geosciences Bureau (DENR) — source of landslide susceptibility maps and geohazard assessments.
GLOSSARY.HoPE: Head of the Procuring Entity — must confirm in writing the grounds for emergency negotiated procurement.
GLOSSARY.CBEWS: Community-based early warning system — local gauges, observers and alarms run with BDRRMCs.

ROLES.desc: Contact point for assisting agencies: PCG, BFP, PNP, AFP, the private sector and NGOs.

ro: Convene the CDRRMC for the PDRA and decide the warning posture.
Sign the evacuation order or EO; confirm the delegation of authority to the IC.
Back the IC; request augmentation through RDRRMC 8 when local capacity is exceeded.
Act on the CDRRMC recommendation on declarations; direct the transition to recovery.
eoc: Raise the EOC alert level and staff the Operations Center.
Push warnings to all 85 BDRRMCs; confirm acknowledgement.
Consolidate SitReps every reporting cycle on the RDRRMC 8 harmonized template.
Shift from response tracking to RDANA and recovery reporting.
ic: Receive the ICS 201 briefing; confirm your delegation of authority.
Set incident objectives (ICS 202) with life safety first.
Organize Operations; keep span of control at 3–7 per supervisor.
Approve the demobilization plan; lead the after-action review.
sofr: Identify the hazards responders will face; check PPE and equipment.
Issue the safety message (ICS 208) before teams deploy.
Watch for fatigue and unsafe acts; you may stop work on the spot.
Document responder injuries and near-misses for the AAR.
pio: Translate the PAGASA/PHIVOLCS warning into plain Cebuano/Waray and English.
Issue one verified advisory per update; name the barangays affected.
Run rumor control; release only figures verified by Planning.
Inform families on assistance, re-entry and claims.
lofr: List agency representatives and their contact numbers.
Bring cluster leads (CSWDO, CHO, PNP, BFP, PCG) into one coordination line.
Route augmentation offers through the EOC; avoid self-deployment.
Thank and release assisting agencies in order.
osc: Pre-position rescue teams and vehicles at safe staging areas.
Organize evacuation by barangay group; assign team leaders.
Assign tactical resources by priority: life safety, incident stability, property.
Scale down tactical operations; move teams to recovery tasks.
psc: Gather hazard maps, population exposure and the PDRA results.
Track resources (ICS 211) and evacuees by barangay.
Prepare the IAP for the next operational period; keep the ICS 214 logs.
Compile documentation for the AAR and the 45-day reporting where required.
lsc: Check fuel, generators, radios and stockpiles of relief goods.
Open evacuation center logistics: food, water, sleeping kits, sanitation.
Supply teams in the field; run the communications plan (ICS 205).
fsc: Confirm the fund source: AA line, LDRRMF 70% or QRF.
Set up cost tracking and time records for responders.
Process emergency procurement under the applicable rules.
Close cost reports; prepare liquidation and claims.

REFERENCES: Philippine DRRM Act. Creates the CDRRMC and CDRRMO (Sec. 12). Sec. 15: the BDRRMC leads if one barangay is affected, the City DRRMC if two or more barangays, the province if two or more cities/municipalities, the region if two or more provinces, the NDRRMC if two or more regions; higher councils support LGUs. Sec. 16: state of calamity; Sec. 21: LDRRMF 70/30.

Implementing guidelines on ICS as the on-scene disaster response and management mechanism. The Responsible Official (the Local Chief Executive) delegates authority to the Incident Commander.
NDRRMC Memo No. 131, s. 2018

Establishment, operationalization and management of EOCs. Five activation triggers; five functions (Management, Operations, Planning, Logistics, Finance/Admin); EOC links clusters (resource providers) and the IMT (resource employer); all IMT resource requests go through the EOC; EOC and ICP shall not be co-located; the IC recommends termination for the RO's approval.
NDRRMC Memo Nos. 43 & 44, s. 2016
Interoperability of IMTs and Response Clusters; mobilization of IMTs.
NDRRMC Memo No. 17, s. 2014
Institutionalizes the Pre-Disaster Risk Assessment (PDRA).
NDRRMC MC No. 19, s. 2016
Management of the Dead and Missing.
RA 12287 (approved 12 Sep 2025) and IRR

State of Imminent Disaster. RDRRMC answers an LDRRMC request within 24 h; the LCE declares and lifts by EO on RDRRMC recommendation. Lifted when the hazard occurs or the forecast impact does not materialize. LGUs may also act early at their own discretion. AA from no more than 10% of the 70% LDRRMF (plus STF, donor, ODA funds); disbursement up to 30% beyond 3 days lead time, up to 70% within 3 days. Report to OCD within 45 days of lifting.

Harmonized Disaster Response Reporting Template and SOP. Alert levels White/Blue/Red; pre-, during-, post-disaster and terminal reports; Forms A–L; LGU reports at 06:00/18:00 (White) and 09:00/19:00 (Blue and Red).
RDRRMOC SOPG (2022 edition), OCD Region VIII
Regional Operations Center procedures: White/Blue/Red alert; EPR protocols Standby–ALPHA–BRAVO–CHARLIE for slow-onset hazards; initial report within 2 hours; criteria for reportable incidents.
Ligtas Pinoy Centers Act — dedicated, resilient evacuation centers.

Implementing guidelines for managing mass casualty incidents.
New Government Procurement Act; replaced RA 9184. Keeps negotiated procurement for emergency cases.

TCWS Nos. 1–5; Heavy Rainfall Warning: Yellow 7.5–15 mm/h, Orange 15–30 mm/h, Red above 30 mm/h; PEIS I–X; tsunami information.

Automatic price freeze on basic necessities in areas declared under a state of calamity.
Ormoc City CDRA (CDRA_Ormoc)
Hazard, exposure and risk by barangay for flood, rain-induced landslide, storm surge and ground shaking; event history (1991 Uring, 2013, 2017 earthquake, 2018–2022 typhoons).
Ormoc City DRRM Ten-Year Plan 2023–2032
Adopted by SP Res. No. 2023-112. 46 barangays with critical flood risk (59,545 people); 24/7 EOC in place but needs an SOP/manual; ICS, EOC management and MDM training needs.
